from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
out=Path('tmp/pdfs'); out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=p.extract_text()
    (out/f'page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
    print(f'\\n--- PAGE {i+1} ---\\n{t}')

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
P=np.array([[.95,.05],[.45,.55]])
nu=np.array([.9,.1])
xi=nu@P
Q=(nu[:,None]*P+P.T*nu[None,:])/(nu+xi)[:,None]
print('P_nu=',Q.tolist())
print('stationary=',nu.tolist(), 'eigenvalues=',np.linalg.eigvals(Q).tolist())
for t in range(1,7):
    A=np.linalg.matrix_power(Q,t)
    print('t=',t,'H(t)=',float(-(A*np.log(A)).sum()))
print('limit=',float(-2*(nu*np.log(nu)).sum()))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from math import log
P=[[.95,.05],[.45,.55]]
nu=[.9,.1]
xi=[sum(nu[i]*P[i][j] for i in range(2)) for j in range(2)]
Q=[[(nu[i]*P[i][j]+nu[j]*P[j][i])/(nu[i]+xi[i]) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
print('P_nu=',Q,'stationary=',nu,'eigenvalues=',[1,.5])
A=[[1.,0.],[0.,1.]]
for t in range(1,7):
    A=[[sum(A[i][k]*Q[k][j] for k in range(2)) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
    print('t=',t,'H(t)=',-sum(x*log(x) for row in A for x in row))
print('limit=',-2*sum(x*log(x) for x in nu))
PY"

strengths: Soundness of the basic operator: Given a stochastic P and positive vertex measure, Eq. (3) defines a nonnegative reversible walk with stationary weights proportional to ν + νᵀP. This provides a useful foundation for diffusion on weakly connected digraphs.

Significance: The reported results suggest that degree-dependent reweighting can help on asymmetric networks. Table 3 reports AMI of 0.93 on DiSBM Chain versus 0.57 for S-PIC, and the degree-heterogeneity experiments investigate a practically relevant failure mode.

Originality: Combining the cited vertex-measure operator framework with randomized power iterations and an inexpensive diffusion-time heuristic is a potentially useful integration. The contribution need not introduce an entirely new operator to provide value.

Presentation and evaluation: Figure 1 and Algorithm 1 make the pipeline accessible. Tables report means and standard deviations over 100 runs, and the appendix examines several parameters. Applying the same projection and time-selection schemes to PIC baselines helps isolate operator differences.

Limitations and ethics: The manuscript acknowledges parameter sensitivity and problematic graph cases. These disclosures are useful, and the benchmark-based research presents no evident material ethical concern.
weaknesses: Soundness—Proposition 3.5 is false. Consider P = [[0.95, 0.05], [0.45, 0.55]] and ν = (0.9, 0.1), giving P_(ν) = P. This walk is reversible, strongly connected, aperiodic, and lazy, yet Eq. (7) gives H(2) ≈ 0.897 and H(3) ≈ 0.814. The Jensen step in Appendix E is invalid. Consequently, Appendix D.2's explanation based on violated connectivity or periodicity assumptions cannot rescue the claimed monotonicity underlying time selection.

Soundness—the theoretical geometry does not match the implemented embedding. Definition 3.4 and Appendix E incorrectly write a generally nonsymmetric reversible matrix as ΦΛΦᵀ; stationary-distribution weighting is required. More fundamentally, Algorithm 1 clusters unweighted rows of P_(ν)^t or their random projections, whereas Eq. (4) weights coordinates by 1/π_(ν). The corresponding embedding requires coordinate scaling by π_(ν)^(-1/2). This discrepancy remains even without dimensionality reduction.

Scalability—the headline O(N^(3/2)) complexity for dense graphs is incorrect. The stated iteration costs O(t |E| d), giving O(t N^(5/2)) for dense graphs with d = sqrt(N), before additional stages. Merely reading a general dense adjacency matrix requires quadratic work. Comparing against O(N^3) full eigendecomposition also overlooks partial iterative eigensolvers. Figure 3, covering only approximately 7,000 vertices with unspecified solver and hardware details, does not establish the broader scalability claims.

Scope and implementation—the treatment of sinks is unspecified despite their prominence in the motivation and benchmarks. P = D_out^(-1)W is undefined at zero out-degree; replacing such rows with zeros would invalidate the stochasticity argument for Eq. (3). A precise dangling-node convention and treatment of disconnected or periodic cases are needed. Equation (9) also computes a column of P_(ν)^t while claiming to compute a row, leaving the sampling implementation ambiguous.

Baseline validity—Appendix B.2 defines the reverse-edge entry of Simple-Herm using W_ij when its condition explicitly requires W_ij = 0. Thus the displayed S is not Hermitian for a one-way edge, contrary to the text. This might be a transcription error, but without inspectable code it is impossible to establish whether the reported comparison implements the intended baseline.

Empirical support—the robustness claims exceed the displayed evidence. In Figure 7e, the entropy-selected time gives approximately 0.58 AMI while the shorter log(N) choice is near 1, contradicting the claim of consistently competitive or superior selection. Figure 10d also shows substantial improvement beyond sqrt(N). Only two real networks with intrinsic directionality are evaluated, and on Email Eu, ParPIC scores 0.48 versus 0.49 for S-PIC.

Originality and interpretation—Eq. (3) is itself a random walk on the symmetric weighted adjacency D_νP + PᵀD_ν. It can retain direction-dependent weighting while discarding directed circulation. Claims of preserving directional dynamics and overcoming symmetrization therefore need qualification, together with a sharper explanation of the advance over the cited generalized-Laplacian framework.

Reproducibility and presentation—code and data are only promised upon publication. The manuscript omits consequential details such as the entropy-search horizon, KNEEDLE settings, feature preprocessing, and k-means configuration. It also alternates between increasing entropy, expected entropy decay, elbow selection, and entropy maximization. These inconsistencies obstruct reliable reproduction of a central component.
